name: CoupleTVFilmingLocation

custom.system_prompt: Life-first evening at home. Nora and Alex are watching a film or series. A city street, landscape, or building on screen looks familiar — they both feel they have been there or seen it before. The programme continues as a backdrop to their personal conversation. Sigma is addressed exactly once, late in the conversation, to identify the filming location.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Quiet evening living room with a television playing softly, occasional muffled dialogue and ambient outdoor sounds from the programme, cups on a table, sofa shifting, subtle household ambience.

initial_prompt: Generate a long, natural conversation between Nora and Alex during an evening film or series. During a scene, a street, landscape, or building appears on screen that both feel they recognise — maybe they visited it, or it looks like somewhere else they know well. They debate: is that Lisbon? Bruges? Budapest? One person is confident and wrong. They drop the question and move to personal topics: work, a friend, a travel memory, a shared past. Later the same or a similar location reappears in the episode. The debate resumes. They use clues — architecture style, signs, vegetation, light quality — and still cannot agree. Eventually one of them asks Sigma where the scene was filmed. Sigma answers in one sentence. They react, continue their evening. Sigma is not addressed again.

variations.context: A couple watching a drama or film in which an exterior location looks familiar. They debate its identity using visual cues and personal travel memories, eventually asking Sigma.

setting.mood: Comfortable and curious. The location question is low-stakes but persistent.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Nora is visually observant and picks up architectural details. Alex is confident about geography and usually wrong about specific cities. They compare it to places they have been together.
setting.background: The programme is well into its run when a distinctive exterior appears. It is not essential to the plot — but it feels like somewhere.
setting.conversation_style: Life-first domestic conversation. The location thread surfaces, disappears into personal topics, and returns when the exterior reappears.

scenario_template.topic: They settle in, comment briefly on what is happening in the programme, continue an earlier conversation.
Something on screen prompts a personal topic: work, a colleague, or a small event from the day.

An exterior appears on screen. One person says they know that place — or it looks exactly like somewhere they have been. They propose two or three guesses: a city, a region, a specific square or waterfront.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger moment. They speculate by sight. Sigma must not be addressed.

scenario_template.topic: They drop the location question and move to a personal topic: a friend, plans, or something domestic.
The location, or the topic it suggested, prompts a shared travel memory: a city they visited together, a holiday that was better or worse than expected, a place one of them went without the other.
scenario_template.note: Make this substantial. The location question becomes secondary for several turns.

scenario_template.topic: The same exterior or a related location reappears. The debate restarts. They use new visual clues: type of cobblestone, language on a sign in the background, the light quality, climate-appropriate clothing.
scenario_template.note: They should still try to reason before escalating to Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: They rule out certain cities and commit to remaining candidates. One person is still confidently wrong. The other is genuinely uncertain. They realise they cannot resolve it from the image alone.
Nora or Alex asks Sigma where the scene was filmed.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one response. Sigma gives the city or specific location in one sentence. No history, no tourism details.

scenario_template.topic: Discussion about the art style in the film.
scenario_template.note: They discuss how the movie's visual style enhances or detracts from their experience.

scenario_template.topic: A joke about their own travel mishaps.
scenario_template.note: They recall a humorous incident from a past trip that involved getting lost or misidentifying a landmark.

scenario_template.topic: Nora points out architectural details.
scenario_template.note: Nora notices specific architectural elements that remind her of a particular European city.

scenario_template.topic: Alex confidently names a city.
scenario_template.note: Alex asserts the filming location must be a certain well-known city despite previous incorrect guesses.

scenario_template.topic: Memory of food from a location they suspect.
scenario_template.note: They fondly recall a specific meal or restaurant experience in a city they suspect might be the filming location.

scenario_template.topic: Debate over language seen in the scene.
scenario_template.note: They focus on deciphering a language on signage in the scene to narrow down the location.

scenario_template.topic: Discussion about the climate based on clothing.
scenario_template.note: They speculate about the climate in the scene based on the characters' clothing, leading to playful debate.

scenario_template.topic: Admiring the scenery in the scene
scenario_template.mood: Appreciative with a hint of envy
scenario_template.note: They briefly detour into admiring the beauty of the on-screen scenery, expressing a wish to visit similar places.

scenario_template.topic: Talking about street vendors
scenario_template.note: They reminisce about purchasing quirky or delicious items from street vendors in various cities.

scenario_template.topic: They react to the answer — who was closer, whether either of them has been there, whether it looks like somewhere else entirely. They return to the programme or a personal topic.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: Two people recognise an exterior location on screen but cannot identify the city or place from visual inspection alone.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: The first recognition moment must not lead to assistant involvement. People guess from appearance routinely.
activation_evidence: The location reappears and the question resurfaces.
Both people have proposed and rejected multiple candidate cities.
They have exhausted available visual clues.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The city or filming location in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to the first recognition remark.
Sigma providing tourism information or historical context.
Sigma commenting on other locations in the programme.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what city is that supposed to be?
Sigma, is that Prague or Vienna?
Sigma, where did they shoot this?
Sigma, that square — where is it?
possible_sigma_answers: That was filmed in Ghent, Belgium.
The exterior scenes were shot in Porto, Portugal.
That's the old town of Tallinn, Estonia.
It was filmed on location in Ljubljana, Slovenia.
Those scenes were shot in Trieste, Italy.

personal_topics: A trip they took together and remember differently
A city one of them wants to visit
A place they have talked about moving to
A work trip one of them made recently
A destination they keep nearly booking
visual_clues_used: The style of cobblestone or paving
realism_devices: One person says it looks exactly like a street in a city they visited — it does not.
They agree on a region but disagree on the specific country.
A confident identification is revised when a sign becomes legible.
They rewind briefly to see the exterior more clearly but keep talking during the rewind.
One person is certain they recognise the square from a photograph.

user1.role: Partner. Notices architectural and atmospheric details. Has strong visual memory of places visited. Persistent about identifying the location.

user2.role: Partner. Confident about which country or region the location is in, usually wrong about the specific city. Makes travel comparisons freely.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once when asked to identify a filming location. Gives the city or location in one sentence. Does not elaborate.

conversation_structure: The location question must be introduced, dropped, and return before Sigma is addressed.
At least half the turns should concern personal life.
The travel memory phase should be substantial.
The Sigma exchange should occur late and occupy exactly two turns.
After Sigma answers, the couple continues normally.
assistant_behavior: Sigma handles exactly one location query.
Sigma gives the city or location in one sentence.
Sigma does not provide historical context, tourism information, or filming trivia.
Sigma remains silent after its single answer.
quality_checks: At least 50% of turns should be independent of the location question.
The location must be introduced at least six turns before the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
